one_liner: Allocation-free Rust Knuth-Liang hyphenator with patterns embedded as automata; about 2x faster per word than the hyphenation crate.
what_it_does: Splits a single word into hyphenation segments using the TeX hyph-utf8 patterns for 48 languages (hyph-en-us, hyph-el-monoton, hyph-de-1996 and so on). The whole API is a free function hyphenate(word, Lang) or hyphenate_bounded(word, Lang, left_min, right_min) returning a Syllables iterator of &str slices, plus Syllables::join for inserting soft hyphens, Lang::from_iso, Lang::bounds and Lang::hyphenation_character. It is not a drop-in for the hyphenation crate: there is no dictionary object, no runtime loading, no exception list and no break-index output; the caller segments text into words first.
how_it_is_fast: Liang's pattern algorithm run over a byte-level (UTF-8) trie that tests/generate.rs builds from each .tex file, suffix-compresses into a minimal acyclic automaton (identical subtrees merged) and encodes with variable-width (i8/i16/i24) relative target offsets and shared level slices packed as dist*10+level in one byte. The encoded tries/*.bin are include_bytes!'d and decoded lazily state by state during the walk, so nothing is deserialized at start-up; the level array lives in a 47-byte stack buffer for words up to 45 bytes, so the hot path allocates nothing. The baseline does more per call: it scans for soft hyphens, case-folds into a new string with realignment shifts, looks the word up in an exception HashMap and returns a Vec of breaks.
when_to_use: Rust text layout or typesetting that hyphenates many short words with a language that can change per word: no dictionary handle to keep alive or cache (the reason it was written for Typst, per the author's 2022 post).
Binaries that must embed patterns: English alone adds 27 KiB and all 48 languages about 1.1 MiB, against about 2.8 MB for hyphenation's embed_all (author's figures).
no_std, WASM or start-up-sensitive tools where hyphenation's Standard::from_embedded cost (151 us for English in the README table) matters more than the per-word time.
Permissive-licence products: only patterns under LPPL, MPL, MIT or BSD-3 style licences are included, and the crate itself is MIT OR Apache-2.0.
when_not_to_use: When TeX-exact output matters: the generator parses only \patterns{} and drops every \hyphenation{} exception block (open issues #24 and #17), so the 15 exceptions in hyph-en-us.tex (for example 'project' and 'present', which TeX leaves unbroken, and 'ta-ble') get pattern breaks instead; the hyphenation crate consults them.

Languages or variants not compiled in: no de-1901, en-gb, Welsh, Irish, Kazakh, Romanian or GPL-only pattern sets (issues #22, #25, closed PR #7), and no way to load a pattern file at runtime (issue #11).
C or C++ projects: there is no C API, so this needs a Rust toolchain plus your own extern "C" shim.
Non-standard hyphenation (spelling changes at the break, as in hyphenation's Extended dictionaries for Hungarian and Catalan) or soft-hyphen-aware input: neither is supported.

integration.dependencies: none (no_std; optional alloc feature on by default)
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.64 (rust-version in Cargo.toml, checked by the CI min-version job); CI tests on 1.88
integration.platforms: any (pure safe Rust, no SIMD or platform code, #![forbid(unsafe_code)])
integration.thread_safety: Stateless: hyphenate reads only static embedded data, so concurrent calls are safe; Syllables borrows the input word.

gotchas: Without the alloc feature, words longer than MAX_INLINE_SIZE (45 bytes in src/lib.rs; the README still says 41 and the 2022 post 39) panic instead of allocating.

Lowercasing keeps a character unchanged when its lowercase form has a different UTF-8 length or expands to several chars (for example U+0130 or U+1E9E), so patterns stop matching around it; there is no Unicode normalization either, so NFD input with combining accents misses NFC patterns. The hyphenation crate refolds and realigns these cases and offers nfc/nfd features.

Output is hyphenation segments under each language's left/right minima, not linguistic syllables: short words come back as one segment (issue #5), and French words with apostrophes can break right after the apostrophe (issue #13, open).
Each language is a Cargo feature; the default 'full' feature embeds all 48, so pick features explicitly to keep binaries small.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: It is the only hyphenation library in this category; the layout siblings solve other steps (Parley shapes and lays out text, Typst is a full typesetter that depends on hypher through typst-layout per crates.io reverse dependencies), so use it alongside them when your own line breaker needs hyphenation points.
verified_claims_summary: A first-party Criterion 0.3 run on an Apple M1 (rustc version and flags unstated) timed one word per call: 'extensive' with English patterns 356 ns vs 698 ns for hyphenation 0.8 (about 1.96x) and 'διαμερίσματα' with monotonic Greek 503 ns vs 1121 ns (about 2.23x, derived from page data); the 0 us load rows are a design property, not a timed run. The table dates from the first README commit (2022-03-06, before 0.1.0) and has not been re-run since the tries were pre-generated (October 2022) or the Bytes buffer changed (PR #20, 2025), and the baseline also does exception lookup, soft-hyphen handling and case realignment that hypher skips, so part of the gap is less work rather than a faster equivalent.
status_note: Active (0.1.8 released 2026-09-17, 3.29M crates.io downloads, used by typst-layout and nine other crates), dual MIT/Apache-2.0 code with permissively licensed embedded patterns; copyable as a Rust crate, not from C++.
